A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Singular Bayesian Neural Networks and contain readable main text and Appendices A–I. The text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, forecasting, and OOD experiments in Section 4, with extended analyses, image classification experiments, and toy regression in Appendices H–I.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and appendix results, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and toy regression.

M1.justification: The factorization, variational objective, sampling, initialization, and MLP/LSTM/Transformer implementations are unchanged. Appendix E revises guarantees for the same predictor.

E1.justification: Both retain MIMIC-III adult/newborn evaluation, Beijing/Guangzhou forecasting and OOD evaluation, SST-2/AG News, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and synthetic regression.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods, including deterministic models, five-member Deep Ensembles, Full-Rank BBB, LR-SVD, and Rank-1 multiplicative models. Appendix I's Gaussian and Laplace comparisons also match.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, architectures, training budgets, metrics, and Monte Carlo evaluation settings in Section 4 and Appendices G–I are unchanged.

E4.justification: The rank/KL sensitivity analyses, singular-value analyses, selective prediction, uncertainty-score comparisons, calibration-binning checks, and regression uncertainty case study are retained without changed evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, mean and standard deviation reporting, and statistical qualifications are unchanged. No uncertainty estimation procedure or significance test is added.

E6.justification: Experimental scores and plotted findings match throughout. Examples include Low-Rank MIMIC-III AUC-OOD 0.802 in Table 1, SST-2 accuracy 0.806 in Table 3, and regression MC-200 RMSE 0.50296 in Table 19.

T1.justification: Appendix E.10 adds a convex-loss assumption and replaces v1's faulty conditioning argument with a Jensen-based derivation. Approach B now uses the conditional good-event predictor's empirical loss instead of the full predictor's loss. E.17–E.21 also replace the unspecified first-layer norm with the class supremum B1, bounded by sqrt(r1) C1, and propagate this through the bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about singular posteriors, structured correlations, parameter efficiency, generalization guarantees, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: Appendix E corrects the interpretation of first-layer rank dependence, qualifies bound comparisons by their constants, and explains why the high-probability extension needs convexity or additional tail control. E.23 also adds a claim that near-deterministic posteriors make the PAC-Bayes gap vanish. Empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Remark E.30 explains estimating the conditional predictor through rejection sampling, retaining posterior samples satisfying spectral-norm bounds. Existing implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and experimental inference disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained, including Appendix A's comparisons with mean-field, covariance-factorization, perturbation, and Bayesian LoRA approaches.

P1.justification: Appendix E.9–E.11 receives targeted rewriting and expanded explanations of conditional predictors and bound comparisons. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain stable, with minor date and capitalization edits.

P2.justification: Appendix figures and tables shift relative to surrounding text. For example, Figure 9 moves from page 48 to 49, and Figures 18–19 move before the Appendix I heading. Existing plots, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: E.17 and E.10 improve class-uniform bounds and replace faulty conditioning with an explicit Jensen argument. However, v2 newly claims that standard losses satisfy its globally bounded convex-loss assumption (E.28), conflicting with their formulas in C.5, and that near-deterministic posteriors make the PAC-Bayes gap vanish (E.23), which does not follow from the KL-based bound. These corrections and new validity problems leave the net quality direction unclear; empirical evidence is unchanged.
